Controller guide | Step 1 of 9

Prepare one controller VM

You need a prepared Linux server first. Ask your server team to confirm the items in the picture. The app installer does not install Docker or Python.

Use RHEL 9 or Ubuntu 26.04. Keep SELinux enabled. Reserve UID/GID 10001 for the dedicated application account.

Fresh machine: complete the matching command sheets on pages 10-13 first. They install the app; then continue at Step 4 for browser login. Product settings stay in the GUI. Native OS and DC tests remain pending.

Controller guide | Step 2 of 9

Make three connections available

Ask the network team for a fixed IP, a stable name, correct time and trusted HTTPS. The installer needs approved image/package download access; this is not an offline installer.

The installer does not open host firewall ports. Keep backend, database and cluster ports private. An approved load balancer can provide different public URLs.

Controller guide | Step 3 of 9

Run the controller installer

Already completed command sheets 10-13? The controller is installed. Skip this installer command and go to Step 4. Otherwise run it only once after preparing dependencies and files.

Ask your release/server team for prthak-controller-0.16.0.tar.gz. They must verify its signature, copy it privately and extract it into a protected root-owned folder using independently approved release trust.

Open Terminal in that extracted folder. Paste the command below. If sudo asks for your Linux password, type it and press Enter; the password does not appear on screen.

Paste this command and press Enter
sudo ./scripts/install-controller.sh --gui-setup

Wait for installation to finish. Keep the HTTPS setup URL that it prints. Do not create or edit an .env file.

Controller guide | Step 4 of 9

Sign in and change the password

Open the exact HTTPS URL printed by the installer. Your server team must confirm the certificate identity before you enter credentials.

A fresh installation uses admin / admin. Replace the password with 12 to 256 characters before entering the workspace. Existing installations keep their existing users.

The built-in admin cannot be deleted, disabled, renamed or demoted. Its password can be changed or reset.

Controller guide | Step 5 of 9

Finish the platform settings

Click Platform settings → Setup. Use Site & cluster settings for this node, then HTTPS certificates to prepare the permanent application name and approved certificate.

Use the Storage tab for the data location. Default: /var/lib/prthak. Mount storage first; moving active data uses the reviewed GUI operation.

Leave workers on AUTO. Start with one standalone node. It runs the controller/router with SQLite; PostgreSQL HA is a separate three-voter setup stage.

Controller guide | Step 6 of 9

Choose who may use the app

Click Users & access. As Super Admin, add the named people who will use Prṛthak and select their role.

You may start with local accounts. Configure optional SAML here, or Microsoft Entra through Platform settings → Setup. SSO needs your identity team and explicitly provisioned users.

Users change their own local password through the top-right account menu. Only Super Admin manages other users and roles.

Controller guide | Step 7 of 9

Set the update interval

Click Platform settings → Agent polling. Start with 30 seconds for policy control and 900 seconds for the full inventory fallback.

Preview affected servers, save the settings, then check their applied polling status. Later you can change the whole fleet or selected groups/tags here.

Agents pull new policies automatically. Polling includes timing variation and network work; a saved setting is not a guaranteed completion time.

Controller guide | Step 8 of 9

Confirm the dashboard is ready

Check: trusted HTTPS opens, your new password works, and controller readiness is healthy. Keep the printed URL and the new password in your approved records.

Next: create your real locations in Locations, then follow the separate Agent installation guide. Servers appear after installation and their first authenticated report.

Create a backup schedule in Platform settings → Backups. Back up private trust/identity material separately as required by the recovery procedure.

An empty server list is normal before agents connect. Do not add example records to make the dashboard look populated.

Controller guide | Step 9 of 9

If something does not work

No dashboard? Ask the server team to check installation completion, Docker, the address, HTTPS trust and TCP 8787 access.

Need help preparing Linux? Share the prerequisite page and the official Docker RHEL/Ubuntu instructions linked in the browser guide. The one app command assumes that preparation is complete.

This guide explains the current code and GUI. Your native RHEL/Ubuntu validation, actual 20-server pilot and DC/DR tests remain separate deployment work.

Command sheet 1 of 4 | Choose this page OR the Ubuntu page

Prepare a fresh RHEL 9 controller

Run on the new RHEL 9 controller VM. Sign in with your Linux account and sudo access. Use a dedicated systemd VM with approved repositories, fixed IP/DNS, correct time and mounted persistent storage. Keep SELinux enabled. Your server team provides this login and SSH host identity. Run the dependency commands below inside the resulting SSH window.

On your laptop first - replace YOUR_USER and CONTROLLER_IP
ssh YOUR_USER@CONTROLLER_IP
RHEL 9 only - prepare Python and Docker
set -eu
sudo dnf install -y python3 tar curl ca-certificates dnf-plugins-core
sudo dnf config-manager --add-repo \
  https://download.docker.com/linux/rhel/docker-ce.repo
sudo dnf install -y docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io \
  docker-buildx-plugin docker-compose-plugin
sudo systemctl enable --now docker
python3 --version
sudo docker version
sudo docker compose version

Python must be 3.9 or newer; Compose must be v2. If packages conflict with an existing container stack, stop and ask your server team. Do not remove working services to force installation.

Allow approved browser access to 8787 and agent access to 8788/8789. Ask the network team to restrict Docker-published ports and private backends; do not assume ordinary host firewall rules alone protect published container ports. Native RHEL acceptance remains pending.

Command sheet 2 of 4 | Ubuntu 26.04 only

Prepare a fresh Ubuntu controller

Run on the new Ubuntu 26.04 controller VM. Skip this page if you used RHEL. Use a dedicated systemd VM, sudo access and approved download access. The commands add Docker's official package repository. Your server team provides this login and SSH host identity. Run the dependency commands below inside the resulting SSH window.

On your laptop first - replace YOUR_USER and CONTROLLER_IP
ssh YOUR_USER@CONTROLLER_IP
Ubuntu 26.04 only - prepare Python and Docker
set -eu
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y python3 tar ca-certificates curl
sudo install -m 0755 -d /etc/apt/keyrings
sudo curl -fsSL https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/gpg \
  -o /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc
sudo chmod a+r /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc
. /etc/os-release
PRTHAK_DOCKER_ARCH=$(dpkg --print-architecture)
sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.sources >/dev/null <<EOF
Types: deb
URIs: https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu
Suites: $VERSION_CODENAME
Components: stable
Architectures: $PRTHAK_DOCKER_ARCH
Signed-By: /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc
EOF
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io \
  docker-buildx-plugin docker-compose-plugin
sudo systemctl enable --now docker
python3 --version
sudo docker version
sudo docker compose version

If an existing container installation conflicts, stop for review. Keep current firewall protection enabled. Restrict public 8787/8788/8789 and private backends through approved network/Docker controls. Native Ubuntu acceptance remains pending.

Command sheet 3 of 4 | Same process for RHEL and Ubuntu

Copy the controller release to the VM

First obtain prthak-controller-0.16.0.tar.gz from your release administrator. They must approve its signature using independently trusted release identity before transfer. A Git source ZIP is not this installation archive; no GitHub release download URL is assumed.

On your laptop - replace YOUR_USER and CONTROLLER_IP
ssh YOUR_USER@CONTROLLER_IP
In that controller SSH window - create a private upload folder
mkdir -p "$HOME/prthak-media"
chmod 0700 "$HOME/prthak-media"
In a SECOND laptop terminal - replace the file path and address
scp "/PATH/TO/prthak-controller-0.16.0.tar.gz" \
  YOUR_USER@CONTROLLER_IP:prthak-media/

An approved graphical file-transfer tool can do the same copy. Keep the original archive name. Return to the first SSH window for the next page. You do not need Git on the controller.

Command sheet 4 of 4 | Run in the controller SSH window

Check the bytes and install the controller

These checks apply only to the signed 0.16.0 archive supplied with this guide. The checksum detects changed bytes; it does not replace independent signature/publisher approval. Stop if the check does not print OK.

RHEL 9 or Ubuntu 26.04 - protect, check, extract and install
set -eu
sudo install -d -o root -g root -m 0700 /var/tmp/prthak-media
sudo install -o root -g root -m 0600 \
  "$HOME/prthak-media/prthak-controller-0.16.0.tar.gz" \
  /var/tmp/prthak-media/prthak-controller-0.16.0.tar.gz
PRTHAK_SUM=56742a9c77bbef803e6a17bfd048494070db37b8f35d19cdb21bd8995a2f92bb
printf '%s  %s\n' "$PRTHAK_SUM" \
  /var/tmp/prthak-media/prthak-controller-0.16.0.tar.gz \
  | sudo sha256sum -c -
sudo install -d -o root -g root -m 0755 /opt/prthak/releases
sudo tar --no-same-owner --no-same-permissions \
  -xzf /var/tmp/prthak-media/prthak-controller-0.16.0.tar.gz \
  -C /opt/prthak/releases
cd /opt/prthak/releases/prthak-controller-0.16.0
sudo ./scripts/install-controller.sh --gui-setup
sudo systemctl status prthak-appliance-manager.service --no-pager
sudo docker ps

Open the printed HTTPS setup URL after verifying certificate trust. A fresh empty installation uses admin / admin and forces a password change. Finish settings in the GUI; no manual .env file is needed. Initial setup uses SQLite; PostgreSQL HA is a separate later stage.
